newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea says will not intervene in Kia takeover.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea says will not intervene in Kia takeover.

text.p: The South Korea government has not and will never intervene in any takeover bid, including anything involving Kia Group, or industrial restructuring programmes by private companies, the finance minister said on Tuesday.

In a meeting with Kia creditors on Tuesday morning, Finance Minister Kang Kyong-shik brushed aside public suspicions that the government has been directly or indirectly seeking a third party to take over the beleaguered Kia Group.
"In conclusion, the government had never discussed the issue. And the government has no intention and will never interevene in any takeover bid or industrial restructuring programme," Kang said.
He said government intervention was prohibited under the rules of the World Trade Organisation.
Kang said the government needed to clarify its stance to eliminate "public worries and unnecessary misunderstandings" related to Kia.
He said creditors were trying to help Kia survive by supporting its self-rescue plans, including spinning off affiliates.
The government would reform related regulations so that companies could restructure their businesses more efficiently, he added.
"So, I believe a (Kia) takeover by a third party looks unlikely to materialise under the current administration," Kang said.
Creditor banks to the nation's eighth largest conglomerate on Monday agreed to grant 183.1 billion won in emergency loans to Kia's core affiliates but only under conditions.
They also agreed the bailout period for Kia would continue until September 29 without condition. During the period, the group would be exempted from servicing debts.
"The government believes creditors made the right decision and fully supports it," Kang said.
"The government hopes Kia's self-rescue plan will be implemented smoothly in cooperation with creditors, and the government wants Kia to be normalised as soon as possible," he added.
